intro.title: Build typed error hierarchy classes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a hierarchy of custom error classes using TypeScript. You'll learn how to create a base error class and extend it to define more specific error types, like a 'ValidationError' or 'NetworkError'. The core concept is using class inheritance to structure errors in a way that makes them easier to catch and handle in your code. You'll work with TypeScript features such as classes, the 'extends' keyword, and custom constructors. By the end, you'll have a reusable error system that improves the reliability and clarity of your applications.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, typed error hierarchies are essential for handling different failure scenarios in a structured way. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, you might have specific error classes for payment failures (PaymentError), inventory issues (InventoryError), and shipping problems (ShippingError), each with their own properties and recovery logic. This pattern allows developers to catch and handle errors precisely in different UI components like checkout forms, order management panels, or inventory modals. By creating a hierarchy of typed errors, you ensure consistent error handling across your application while providing clear debugging information and user-friendly error messages.
